meaning: let's ~ ; why don't we ~ (a rousing call to joint action)

exercises.example_sentence: 困難な時こそ、みんなで力を合わせて頑張ろうではないか。
exercises.translation: It is precisely in hard times that we should all join forces and press on together. (rallying a group)
wrong_choice_explanations: 頑張るではないか after the plain form is an exclamation of something noticed — 'why, they're pressing on!' — not an invitation; rallying everyone to join forces needs the volitional 頑張ろう before ではないか.
頑張るのではないか voices a guess or rhetorical claim, 'isn't it in hard times that we press on?'; it comments on what people do rather than calling the group to act now.
頑張ろうとも is concessive, 'even if we press on…', and needs a main clause after it; the sentence ends there, so no call to join forces is ever made.

exercises.example_sentence: 今日は無礼講だ。さあ、存分に飲もうではないか。
exercises.translation: Tonight rank is set aside. Come, let's drink to our hearts' content! (a host addressing the gathering)
wrong_choice_explanations: 飲むではないか after the plain form exclaims at something observed — 'why, he's drinking!' — which can't follow さあ; a host urging the room to drink needs the volitional 飲もう.
飲むのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose people will drink'; after さあ and 存分に the host is urging the guests on, not speculating about them.
飲もうとも means 'even if we drink…' and leaves a concession hanging with no main clause; さあ calls for an invitation, not a 'no matter' clause.

exercises.translation: Let us forget the past and live our lives facing forward from here on.
exercises.blank_target: 生きていこうではないか
wrong_choices: 生きていくではないか

wrong_choice_explanations: 生きていくではないか after the plain form is a remark on something noticed, 'why, they are living on!'; after 過去は忘れて the writer is urging readers forward, which needs the volitional 生きていこう.
生きていくのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose we will go on living…'; it predicts rather than urging readers to put the past behind them and face forward.
生きていこうとも is concessive, 'even if we live facing forward…', and needs a main clause to follow; the sentence ends on it, so the appeal to readers never lands.

取り組むのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose they'll take on reform'; 今こそ and 会社の未来のために frame an appeal to act now, not a prediction.
取り組もうとも means 'even if we take on reform…' and needs a main clause; left at the end of the sentence, it never tells anyone to act.

wrong_choice_explanations: 始めるではないか after the plain form is an exclamation about something noticed, 'why, they're starting!'; urging each person to begin with what they can do needs the volitional 始めよう.
始めるのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose each person will start…'; the writer is calling on readers to act for the environment, not predicting their behaviour.
始めようとも is concessive, 'even if we each start…', and needs a main clause; the sentence stops there, so the call to start never comes.

exercises.blank_target: 挑戦しようではないか

wrong_choice_explanations: 挑戦するではないか after the plain form exclaims at something observed — 'why, they're taking it on!' — not an encouragement; urging the team past fear of failure needs the volitional 挑戦しよう.
挑戦するのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose they'll take on something new'; 失敗を恐れず sets up encouragement to the team, not speculation about them.
挑戦しようとも means 'even if we try new things…' and needs a following main clause; the sentence ends on the concession, so no one is urged on.

やり遂げるのではないか is a guess, 'I suppose they'll see it through'; 諦めるのはまだ早い leads into an exhortation, not a prediction.
やり遂げようとも means 'even if we see it through…' and needs a main clause; the speaker stops mid-concession instead of urging the group to finish.

exercises.example_sentence: 意見が違っても、まずは互いの話に耳を傾けようではないか。

wrong_choice_explanations: 傾けるではないか after the plain form is an exclamation about something noticed, 'why, they're listening!'; まずは marks an appeal to listen first, which needs the volitional 傾けよう.
